text:
Oncall-Bot: ALERT: runtime-p99-latency spike detected in production in us-west-2 after recent rollout (rollout_id=rl_2026_03_12_17). Avg p99 increased from 230ms -> 1.8s. 20% of pods showing kernel fallback.
Maya Chen: I'm eyeballing logs now, looks like kernel selectors are preferring a fallback kernel for small batches. seeing messages: "kernel_fallback: true" and repeated "KV cache miss".
Maya Chen: paste logs:
```
2026-03-12T17:11:09Z runtime[gw-42]: kernel_select: chosen=ff... fallback=true seq_len=64 batch=1
2026-03-12T17:11:09Z runtime[gw-42]: kv_cache: miss key=usr-ctx-... size=0
```
AJ Patel: oncall here, thanks. Is this coincident with the canary traffic shift? Rollout id matches last deploy yes.
Maya Chen: yes, canary at 16:55 shifted 15% of prod traffic to v3.4.0-opt. Canary node pools started using new kernel affinity logic.
SRE Jim: assigning sev2 until we confirm customer impact. Any error rates up? Metrics show 2xx still high but latency spike could impact tail-sensitive customers.
Leo García: I'm seeing alerts from monitoring: 5 customer-facing routes with >50% p99 regression, notably embedding service and reranker.
Product Rahul: Which customers might be hit? Any paying customers in APAC on that region?
Maya Chen: quick grep indicates high traffic tenants: acme-inc, dataflow.ai. Acme's health checks show increased timeouts for streaming endpoints.
AJ Patel: immediate actions: 1) Pause rollout / kill feature flag 2) Roll back to previous model variant if pause doesn't drop latency 3) Notify CS for affected customers.
Maya Chen: trying kill-switch now: hitting feature-flag service...
DeployBot: Feature flag update: rollout.v3_kernel_affinity=false by AJ Patel at 2026-03-12T17:18:42Z :white_check_mark:
Maya Chen: toggled. Observability: p99 is dropping on a few pods from ~1.8s -> 340ms, but some pods still at ~900ms.
SRE Jim: looks like partial mitigation. Could be in-flight sessions still using the new kernel. Any kernel-level fallback logs after flag toggle?
Maya Chen: still seeing kernel_fallback logs on the same hosts. Might need to restart those workers to clear incompatible JIT kernels.
Leo García: restarting affected pods in gw-pool-7/zone-usw2b now (rolling restart non-disruptive with drain). Command:
```
kubectl rollout restart ds/runtime-gateway -n prod --field-selector=spec.nodeName=ip-10-0-7-*
```
Maya Chen: restarted 6 pods, initial numbers: p99 back to ~270ms on restarted hosts.
AJ Patel: CS notified: @CS-team we've identified latency spike after today's kernel-affinity change; mitigation in progress, may have affected acme-inc/dataflow.ai. Sending status update.
Product Rahul: please include ETA; customers asking for expected recovery time.
SRE Jim: ETA: 15-25 minutes for full rolling restart to finish and in-flight caches to clear.
Oncall-Bot: Incident created INC-2026-0312-47, severity: P2, owner: AJ Patel. Conference bridge: https://meet.redwood/incident/INC-2026-0312-47
Maya Chen: hypothesis: new kernel affinity causes single-batch workloads to avoid optimized kernels, causing fallback path with higher per-token overhead. Need fix: adjust selector to prefer optimized kernel for batch_size<=4 or revert kernel selection rule.
AJ Patel: next: revert the kernel selector change in rollout branch and prepare hotfix. Who's owner?
Maya Chen: I'll open PR to revert, will include unit test for kernel preference and perf test in canary harness. Tagging @eng-runtime for review.
SRE Jim: keep monitoring. If p99 stays >500ms after restarts, escalate to P1.
Leo García: so far telemetry shows p99 trending to baseline as restarts complete. At 17:43 p99 ~320ms cluster-wide.
AJ Patel: plan to fully rollback rollout if we see new regressions after PR. For now keeping rollout paused. Please log any customer errors and collect request ids for CS.
Maya Chen: collected request IDs for acme-inc: [req_78a, req_78b, req_79c] — dumping to secure channel for CS handoff.
Product Rahul: thanks, CS will reach out proactively.
Oncall-Bot: On-call handoff scheduled: AJ Patel -> Maya Chen at 2026-03-12T18:00Z. Handoff note: monitor INC-2026-0312-47 until resolved.
AJ Patel: thanks team. I'll keep the incident page updated. Kudos to Maya for fast rollback.
Maya Chen: adding retrospective notes to the incident doc: root cause candidate = kernel affinity selector coupled with small-batch traffic pattern. Action items: (1) revert selector in next patch (2) add perf regression test to CI (3) improve canary traffic profile to include tail-sensitive routes.
SRE Jim: closing note: severity downgrade to P3 at 18:10 as metrics stable and CS notified. Will leave incident open for postmortem.
Maya Chen: posting timeline and artifacts shortly.
DeployBot: Rollout paused: rl_2026_03_12_17 by AJ Patel at 2026-03-12T17:21:10Z :white_check_mark:
AJ Patel: good work. If anything new pops up ping here or call bridge.
